content.text:
I found two problems that I proved with tests and three that I could not fully prove. I wrote the test code in a scratchpad at `/tmp/a7poc`, outside the repository, and `git status` shows the audited repo is unchanged. Note that the repo has no `test/` directory, so the files that the code comments cite as measurements (`test/PushGas.t.sol`, `test/TableCap.t.sol`) are not in this snapshot.

Working markers (summary):
[Feynman: Distribution.receive] The clone takes ETH and writes a log. The comment says this works with only 2,300 gas, but the clone first forwards the call to the implementation, and that costs gas before the implementation code runs. **This part was unclear, so I tested it.**
[Feynman: Distribution.distribute] It splits the unreserved balance by the table, in address order. ETH sends have a 100k gas cap. ERC-20 sends have no gas cap and go through the token. **This part was unclear: the token can call the recipient.**
[Socratic: Distribution.sol:149 — why?] Why must `receive` fit in 2,300 gas? So that `transfer`/`send` payers can pay the clone. Does the clone, with its DELEGATECALL, ever fit in 2,300 gas? The test shows that it does not.
[Socratic: Distribution.sol:402 — why?] Why does the ERC-20 branch ignore the gas cap? Because the developer believed that only the token, which the caller picks, can use up gas. A token with a recipient hook breaks that belief.
[Inversion: distribute] (1) A beneficiary at a low vanity address, with an ERC777-style hook that uses up all its gas. (2) A caller who gives distribute too little gas so that honest pushes fail. This fails: after a failed push, the 1/64 gas that remains cannot pay for the escrow storage writes, so the whole transaction reverts. (3) Revert data of megabytes through the token. This fails: the token frame runs out of gas while it copies the data, so distribute only escrows.
[Inversion: acceptOwnership] (1) The old owner fills `_pending` with very large junk `action` bytes. (2) Then `_clearQueue` costs more than the 16.7M gas cap for one transaction. (3) The old owner's real `setBeneficiaries` matures, and anyone can apply it.
[Inversion: DistributionFactory.create] (1) Another address with the same salt prefix: blocked by the prefix check. (2) A shared forwarder as `msg.sender`, so the prefix is not an individual's address: this gets past the check. (3) A copy of the same contract wallet address on another chain: this also gets past the check.

```
FINDING | contract: Distribution | function: receive | bug_class: stipend-receive-oog | group_key: Distribution | receive | stipend-receive-oog
path: legacy payer → payable(clone).transfer/send (2,300 stipend) → PUSH0 proxy DELEGATECALL + impl receive → OutOfGas → transfer reverts / send returns false
assumption: receive() "Must run under a 2,300-gas `transfer` stipend" (Distribution.sol:149)
violation: The clone's DELEGATECALL (2,600 cold / 100 warm) plus the impl dispatch, the `self` check and the LOG2 need more than 2,300 gas.
proof: Scratch test at /tmp/a7poc/test/P.t.sol, Q.t.sol (repo foundry.toml settings: solc 0.8.34, via_ir, cancun). The trace shows `[2300] clone::receive{value: 1 ether}() ← [OutOfGas]` for both `transfer` (the payer reverts) and `send` (returns false, clone balance stays 0). A gas probe finds that the clone needs stipend + 1,870 = 4,170 gas, even with the implementation already warm.
description: A payer that uses `transfer` or `send` cannot pay any clone, because the clone's `receive` needs about 4,170 gas and the stipend gives 2,300.
fix: Use a clone whose runtime code logs and stops on empty calldata without DELEGATECALL, or remove the 2,300-gas claim and document that `transfer` and `send` fail.

FINDING | contract: Distribution | function: distribute | bug_class: uncapped-token-push-gas | group_key: Distribution | distribute | uncapped-token-push-gas
path: hostile beneficiary (low vanity address, so its row comes first) registers an ERC777-style tokensReceived hook that loops → distribute(hookToken) → token.transfer forwards 63/64 → hook uses all of it → distribute keeps about gasleft/64 → later rows run out of gas → whole distribute reverts, on every call
assumption: "an ERC-20 push is bounded by the token … a hostile token's return data costs only the caller who named it" (Distribution.sol:393-404). Only the ETH branch is capped, because the developer believed only the token can use up gas.
violation: A hook token gives control to the recipient inside `transfer`, and `_push` puts no gas cap on `token.call`.
proof: /tmp/a7poc/test/R.t.sol, hook token, hostile row at 0x1000 first, distribute called with 16,000,000 gas (under the EIP-7825 cap of 16,777,216). With 17 or more rows, distribute reverts. The control (same table, no hostile hook) succeeds with 527,095 gas. A real ERC777 costs more per row, so the threshold is lower. The hostile row cannot be escrowed past, so no row gets the token until the owner replaces the table after `delay`.
description: A beneficiary with a token hook that uses all its gas makes `distribute` for that token revert, so no beneficiary gets that token.
fix: Give the ERC-20 `token.call` in `_push` a gas cap, as the ETH branch has, and copy no more than one word of return data.

LEAD | contract: Distribution | function: acceptOwnership | bug_class: unbounded-queue-clear | group_key: Distribution | acceptOwnership | unbounded-queue-clear
code_smells: `propose` stores `action` bytes of any length with no validation. `_clearQueue` deletes every slot of every entry in one loop, in `acceptOwnership` and in the renounce branch of `transferOwnership`.
description: An owner key that an attacker controls can fill `_pending` until `acceptOwnership` costs more than the gas cap for one transaction, and its own queued `setBeneficiaries` then matures. We did not measure the gas for each slot, and the honest holder of the same key can still `cancel` entries.

LEAD | contract: DistributionFactory | function: create | bug_class: shared-sender-salt-squat | group_key: DistributionFactory | create | shared-sender-salt-squat
code_smells: The prefix check ties `salt` to `msg.sender` only. When the sender is a public forwarder (for example Multicall3, which has the same address on every chain) or a contract wallet with a different holder on another chain, anyone can use that prefix.
description: An attacker who calls through the same forwarder can front-run `create` and own the predicted address with their own table. We did not check whether the dapp ever sends `create` through a forwarder.

LEAD | contract: Distribution | function: distribute | bug_class: double-entry-token-reserve | group_key: Distribution | distribute | double-entry-token-reserve
code_smells: `reserved` is keyed by the token address. A token with two entry points that share one balance shows the escrow of entry A as free balance through entry B.
description: Any caller can split escrowed tokens again through a second entry point of the token, so a later `claim` or `release` for the first entry point reverts. We found no such token in scope.
```

Rejected after tracing (no item emitted):
- **Gas-starving ETH pushes:** the gas that remains after a failed push cannot pay for the escrow storage writes, so the whole transaction reverts.
- **Reentry into `propose`/`applyQueued`:** the `notLocked` modifier blocks it.
- **Desync between `reserved` and `escrowed`:** every write path keeps the two in step.
- **Init and memory restore in the factory's clone code:** both are correct.
- **`App._requireChunk` and the `lock` paths:** both are sound.

proof: Scratch test at /tmp/a7poc/test/P.t.sol, Q.t.sol (repo foundry.toml settings: solc 0.8.34, via_ir, cancun). The trace shows `[2300] clone::receive{value: 1 ether}() ← [OutOfGas]` for both `transfer` (the payer reverts) and `send` (returns false, clone balance stays 0). A gas probe finds that the clone needs stipend + 1,870 = 4,170 gas, even with the implementation already warm.
description: A payer that uses `transfer` or `send` cannot pay any clone, because the clone's `receive` needs about 4,170 gas and the stipend gives 2,300.
fix: Use a clone whose runtime code logs and stops on empty calldata without DELEGATECALL, or remove the 2,300-gas claim and document that `transfer` and `send` fail.

FINDING | contract: Distribution | function: distribute | bug_class: uncapped-token-push-gas | group_key: Distribution | distribute | uncapped-token-push-gas
path: hostile beneficiary (low vanity address, so its row comes first) registers an ERC777-style tokensReceived hook that loops → distribute(hookToken) → token.transfer forwards 63/64 → hook uses all of it → distribute keeps about gasleft/64 → later rows run out of gas → whole distribute reverts, on every call
assumption: "an ERC-20 push is bounded by the token … a hostile token's return data costs only the caller who named it" (Distribution.sol:393-404). Only the ETH branch is capped, because the developer believed only the token can use up gas.
violation: A hook token gives control to the recipient inside `transfer`, and `_push` puts no gas cap on `token.call`.
proof: /tmp/a7poc/test/R.t.sol, hook token, hostile row at 0x1000 first, distribute called with 16,000,000 gas (under the EIP-7825 cap of 16,777,216). With 17 or more rows, distribute reverts. The control (same table, no hostile hook) succeeds with 527,095 gas. A real ERC777 costs more per row, so the threshold is lower. The hostile row cannot be escrowed past, so no row gets the token until the owner replaces the table after `delay`.
description: A beneficiary with a token hook that uses all its gas makes `distribute` for that token revert, so no beneficiary gets that token.
fix: Give the ERC-20 `token.call` in `_push` a gas cap, as the ETH branch has, and copy no more than one word of return data.

LEAD | contract: Distribution | function: acceptOwnership | bug_class: unbounded-queue-clear | group_key: Distribution | acceptOwnership | unbounded-queue-clear
code_smells: `propose` stores `action` bytes of any length with no validation. `_clearQueue` deletes every slot of every entry in one loop, in `acceptOwnership` and in the renounce branch of `transferOwnership`.
description: An owner key that an attacker controls can fill `_pending` until `acceptOwnership` costs more than the gas cap for one transaction, and its own queued `setBeneficiaries` then matures. We did not measure the gas for each slot, and the honest holder of the same key can still `cancel` entries.

LEAD | contract: DistributionFactory | function: create | bug_class: shared-sender-salt-squat | group_key: DistributionFactory | create | shared-sender-salt-squat

LEAD | contract: Distribution | function: distribute | bug_class: double-entry-token-reserve | group_key: Distribution | distribute | double-entry-token-reserve
code_smells: `reserved` is keyed by the token address. A token with two entry points that share one balance shows the escrow of entry A as free balance through entry B.

Named there and read here; never a second opinion. # ---------------------------------------------------------------- scope.tsv, last wins # An absent key gives an absent row. It must # not be a non-zero exit either: `set -e` would turn one absent label into no report at all. scope() { [ -f "$dir/scope.tsv" ] || return 0 awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1==k { v=$2 } END { print v }' "$dir/scope.tsv" } name=$(scope name); [ -n "$name" ] || name='**name missing**' mode=$(scope mode); [ -n "$mode" ] || mode='**Mode missing**' passes_planned=$(scope passes_planned) mem_before=$(scope mem_before) mem_after=$(scope mem_after) mem_sha=$(scope mem_sha) memory_on=0; [ -n "$mem_before" ] && memory_on=1 if [ "$memory_on" = 1 ] && [ ! -f "$dir/memory-before.tsv" ]; then echo "assemble.sh: memory is on but $dir/memory-before.tsv is missing — Turn 5 did not copy it" >&2 memory_on=0 fi # run files in PASS order. "; else printf " · " }' \ | sed -e 's/ · $//' -e 's/
$//') row "**Files reviewed**" "$files" row "**Confidence threshold (1-100)**" "$THRESHOLD" # The Passes cell is COMPOSED from facts, never written as prose by a model. if [ -n "$passes_planned" ] && [ "$passes_planned" -gt 1 ] 2>/dev/null; then short="" for k in $(seq 1 "$passes_planned"); do a=$(scope "pass_${k}_agents"); fail=$(scope "pass_${k}_failed") if [ -n "$fail" ]; then short="${short:+$short, }pass $k failed" elif [ -n "$a" ] && [ "$a" != "12/12" ]; then short="${short:+$short, }pass $k ran $a agents"; fi done if [ "$N" -lt "$passes_planned" ]; then cell="$N of $passes_planned"; else cell="$passes_planned"; fi [ -n "$short" ] && cell="$cell ($short)" row "**Passes**" "$cell" fi [ "$memory_on" = 1 ] && row "**Memory**" "$mem_before records before this scan · $mem_after after · \`$mem_sha\`" [ -n "$broken" ] && row "**Run files**" "$broken" rule say "## Findings" say "" emit_body() { # file bodystart bodyend — copied through, never re-worded awk -v s="$2" -v e="$3" 'NR>=s && NR<=e' "$1" \ | awk '{ lines[++n] = $0 } END { b=1; while (b<=n && lines[b]=="") b++ while (n>=b && lines[n]=="") n-- for (i=b; i<=n; i++) print lines[i] }' } i=0 while IFS=$'\t' read -r k key conf kind agents file pass start end bstart bend title loc lbody memtag; do i=$((i+1)) [ "$title" = "-" ] && title="**Title missing** — the block's title line could not be read" if [ "$loc" = "-" ]; then meta="**location missing**"; else meta="\`$loc\`"; fi say "[$conf] **$i. $title**" say "" meta="$meta · Confidence: $conf" [ "$N" -gt 1 ] && meta="$meta · seen in $k/$N runs" [ -n "$memtag" ] && meta="$meta · $memtag" say "$meta" say "" body=$(emit_body "$file" "$bstart" "$bend") if [ -z "$body" ]; then say "**Body missing** — pass $pass raised this finding and wrote no description." else printf '%s\n' "$body" >> "$R" fi rule done < "$work/findings.tsv" if [ "$nfind" = 0 ]; then # An empty table with a header row and no rows under it is not a report of nothing, it is a # report that looks broken. # Run 1 — solidity-auditor

<!--RUN pass=1 of=1 stamp=20261106-195825 sha=d07483a agents=9/12-->

Pass 1 of 1 · 2026-11-06 · `d07483a` · 9/12 agents returned — the math-precision agent (1) and the invariant agent (5) died on an API safeguard error, and the economic-security agent (3) read its bundle but a safety classifier stopped its output, so it returned no findings.

## Findings

<!--F key=distribution|receive|stipend-receive-oog conf=85 kind=FINDING agents=2-->

[85] **A clone cannot receive ETH from a payer that uses `transfer` or `send`**

`Distribution.receive` · Confidence: 85

**File:** `src/Distribution.sol:146-150` (the promise is at line 146; the clone runtime is written at `src/Distribution.sol:471-474`) · **Severity:** Medium

**Description**
The clone spends 2,600 gas on a cold DELEGATECALL before `receive` runs, so every `transfer` or `send` payment to a clone fails. Two agents reproduced it in scratch Foundry tests: `[2300] clone::receive{value: 1 ether}() ← [OutOfGas]`, and the clone needs about 4,170 gas even when the implementation is warm. A `transfer` payer reverts. A `send` payer that ignores the result keeps the ETH, and no beneficiary is paid.

**Fix**

```diff
-    /// @dev Must run under a 2,300-gas `transfer` stipend, so it does nothing but the guard and the log.
+    /// @dev Does NOT fit a 2,300-gas `transfer`/`send` stipend: the clone's DELEGATECALL alone costs
+    /// 2,600 gas cold. Payers must use `call`, or the clone runtime must log and STOP on empty calldata
+    /// before it delegates (see DistributionFactory.create).
```

<!--/F-->

<!--F key=distributionfactory|create|stipend-receive-oog conf=85 kind=FINDING agents=1-->

[85] **The clone code from `create` delegates plain ETH transfers past the stipend**

`DistributionFactory.create` · Confidence: 85

**File:** `src/Distribution.sol:471-474` (also `predict`, `src/Distribution.sol:490-494`) · **Severity:** Medium

**Description**
`create` deploys a PUSH0 proxy that runs DELEGATECALL for empty calldata, so the 2,300-gas stipend from `transfer` or `send` runs out before `Received` is logged. This is the same root cause as the `Distribution.receive` finding. A scratch PoC passes once a warm-up call touches `implementation` first, so the DELEGATECALL is the cause.

**Fix**

```diff
-            mstore(0x24, 0x5af43d5f5f3e6029573d5ffd5b3d5ff3)
-            mstore(0x14, impl)
-            mstore(0x00, 0x602d5f8160095f39f35f5f365f5f37365f73)
-            distribution := create2(callvalue(), 0x0e, 0x36, salt)
+            // Init code for a runtime that, when CALLDATASIZE == 0, emits Received(CALLER, CALLVALUE)
+            // with LOG2 and STOPs before any DELEGATECALL, and otherwise runs the PUSH0 proxy body
+            // unchanged. `predict` must hash the same bytes. This changes every clone address.
+            distribution := create2(callvalue(), initCodeOffset, initCodeLength, salt)
```

<!--/F-->

<!--F key=distribution|distribute|double-entry-token-reserve conf=80 kind=FINDING agents=4-->

[80] **`distribute` pays out escrow through a second address of the same token**

`Distribution.distribute` · Confidence: 80

**File:** `src/Distribution.sol:155` · **Severity:** Medium

**Description**
Any caller can call `distribute` with the other address of a two-address token, such as CELO's ERC-20, and the table takes the shares escrowed under the first address. Trace on Celo, table A 50% and B 50%, 100 CELO held: `distribute(address(0))` escrows 50 for A, so `reserved[0]` is 50. Then `distribute(CELO)` reads `reserved[CELO] == 0` and splits that 50 again. A's `claim` reverts `ReleaseFailed`, and `distribute(address(0))` underflows until new deposits arrive to cover A's escrow.

**Fix**

```diff
+    /// @dev The ERC-20 form of the native coin on this chain (CELO's GoldToken), or address(0).
+    address private immutable nativeAlias;
@@ function distribute(address token) external nonReentrant {
-        uint256 amount = _balance(token) - reserved[token];
+        uint256 held = reserved[token];
+        if (nativeAlias != address(0) && (token == address(0) || token == nativeAlias)) {
+            held = reserved[address(0)] + reserved[nativeAlias];
+        }
+        uint256 amount = _balance(token) - held;
```

<!--/F-->

<!--F key=distribution|distribute|uncapped-token-push-gas conf=75 kind=FINDING agents=3-->

[75] **A beneficiary with a token hook makes `distribute` fail for every caller**

`Distribution.distribute` · Confidence: 75

**File:** `src/Distribution.sol:166`, push at `src/Distribution.sol:417` · **Severity:** Medium

**Description**
A beneficiary with an ERC-777 `tokensReceived` hook uses up the gas that the ERC-20 push forwards, so `distribute(token)` fails for every caller until the owner changes the table through the timelock. There are two mechanisms. (1) The hook burns all its gas, so the loop keeps only 1/64 of the gas. A scratch PoC with 17 rows reverts at 16M gas, and the same table without the hook needs 527,095 gas. (2) The hook reverts with large return data, and `(ok, data) = token.call(...)` copies all of it into memory with the 1/64 of the gas that is left.

**Fix**

```diff
-        (ok, data) = token.call(abi.encodeWithSelector(TRANSFER, to, amount));
-        ok = ok && (data.length == 0 || (data.length >= 32 && abi.decode(data, (uint256)) == 1));
+        bytes memory cd = abi.encodeWithSelector(TRANSFER, to, amount);
+        uint256 gasCap = TOKEN_PUSH_GAS;
+        assembly ("memory-safe") {
+            mstore(0x00, 0)
+            ok := call(gasCap, token, 0, add(cd, 0x20), mload(cd), 0x00, 0x20)
+            ok := and(ok, or(iszero(returndatasize()), and(gt(returndatasize(), 0x1f), eq(mload(0x00), 1))))
+        }
```

<!--/F-->

<!--F key=distribution|_push|uncapped-token-push-gas conf=75 kind=FINDING agents=3-->

[75] **The ERC-20 branch of `_push` forwards all gas to the token**

`Distribution._push` · Confidence: 75

**File:** `src/Distribution.sol:417` · **Severity:** Medium

**Description**
The ETH branch caps the push at `PUSH_GAS`, but the ERC-20 branch has no cap. A hook token therefore gives the recipient all forwarded gas, and one hostile row can stop `distribute` for that token. The NatSpec at lines 390-401 says "one hostile recipient cannot burn the whole distribution", and the code enforces that only for ETH.

**Fix**

```diff
+    uint256 private constant TOKEN_PUSH_GAS = 100_000;
@@ function _push(address token, address to, uint256 amount, bool keepData)
-        (ok, data) = token.call(abi.encodeWithSelector(TRANSFER, to, amount));
+        // distribute passes keepData == false: cap it so a failed row escrows; release/claim keep full gas.
+        if (keepData) (ok, data) = token.call(abi.encodeWithSelector(TRANSFER, to, amount));
+        else (ok, data) = token.call{gas: TOKEN_PUSH_GAS}(abi.encodeWithSelector(TRANSFER, to, amount));
```

<!--/F-->

<!--F key=distributionfactory|create|unbound-clone-config conf=75 kind=FINDING agents=3-->

[75] **The clone address does not commit to its owner or table**

`DistributionFactory.create` · Confidence: 75

**File:** `src/Distribution.sol:465-474`, `predict` at `src/Distribution.sol:487-498` · **Severity:** Medium

**Description**
The salt holder can deploy the clone on a chain where it is not yet deployed, with the holder's own owner and table, and take the ETH that payers already sent to that address. The address hashes only `0xff‖factory‖salt‖initCodeHash`. `init` accepts funds that arrived before deployment, and the factory is at the same address on every chain through Arachnid CREATE2. The NatSpec at lines 448-453 says "the deploying key never needs to own anything", but the key keeps this power, and anyone who later gets a leaked key gets it too. The gate demoted this finding because only the salt holder can trigger it, and three agents agreeing promoted it back.

**Fix**

```diff
         if (prefix != uint256(uint160(msg.sender))) revert SaltDoesNotStartWith();
+        bytes32 committed = keccak256(abi.encode(salt, owner_, delay_, description_, table_));
@@
-            distribution := create2(callvalue(), 0x0e, 0x36, salt)
+            distribution := create2(callvalue(), 0x0e, 0x36, committed)
@@ predict must take owner_, delay_, description_ and table_ and hash `committed` the same way
```

<!--/F-->

<!--F key=distribution|distribute|reserved-exceeds-balance-underflow conf=75 kind=FINDING agents=5-->

[75] **A balance below `reserved` makes `distribute` revert for every caller**

`Distribution.distribute` · Confidence: 75

**File:** `src/Distribution.sol:155` · **Severity:** Low

**Description**
A negative rebase or an issuer seizure moves the token balance below `reserved[token]`, so `_balance(token) - reserved[token]` panics and the claims that come first take all of the shortfall's cover. Example: `reserved[stETH]` is 1000, a slashing event drops the balance to 990, every `distribute(stETH)` panics 0x11, and the last escrowed account to claim fails. Five agents raised this as a lead, so it is promoted. The fix below only replaces the panic with a clear revert. It does not share the loss between the escrowed accounts.

**Fix**

```diff
-        uint256 amount = _balance(token) - reserved[token];
-        if (amount == 0) revert NothingToDo();
+        uint256 balance = _balance(token);
+        uint256 held = reserved[token];
+        if (balance <= held) revert NothingToDo();
+        uint256 amount = balance - held;
```

<!--/F-->

**Description**
The clone spends 2,600 gas on a cold DELEGATECALL before `receive` runs, so every `transfer` or `send` payment to a clone fails. Two agents reproduced it in scratch Foundry tests: `[2300] clone::receive{value: 1 ether}() ← [OutOfGas]`, and the clone needs about 4,170 gas even when the implementation is warm. +    /// 2,600 gas cold. Payers must use `call`, or the clone runtime must log and STOP on empty calldata
+    /// before it delegates (see DistributionFactory.create).
```

-            mstore(0x14, impl)
-            mstore(0x00, 0x602d5f8160095f39f35f5f365f5f37365f73)
-            distribution := create2(callvalue(), 0x0e, 0x36, salt)

The audit leg ran, but only 9 of its 12 agents returned results. The math-precision and invariant agents died on an API safeguard error, and a safety classifier stopped the economic-security agent's output. Following the skill, none of them was respawned. So this leg has no math-precision, invariant or economic-security coverage as a specialty; other agents covered parts of those areas only along the way.

The run found **8 findings and 7 leads**. The structure check passed (8 findings, and the confidence buckets add up to 8), and `git status` shows no changes in the repo.

**Where the output is:** `.solidity-auditor/runs/20261106-195825/` holds `full-report.md`, `run-1.md` and `scope.tsv`, ready for the runner to collect. I deleted the temporary bundle directory.

**What I added beyond the skill's own output:**
- **A note at the top of `full-report.md`.** On a 1-pass scan the assembler prints no `Passes` row, so without the note the report would say nothing about the 3 lost agents. The note also lists the steps that did not run:
  - **Upstream version check:** skipped, as the leg prompt says.
  - **Model question:** this runtime has no way to ask it, so the agents ran on my own model family, Opus.
- **A `File:` line and a `Severity:` line in every finding body,** because the rollup needs a location and a severity for each one. Every lead also names its file and line.

**Main findings:**
- **Clones cannot receive ETH from `transfer` or `send` (85, Medium).** A clone forwards every call to the implementation, and that cold DELEGATECALL costs 2,600 gas, more than the 2,300-gas stipend. This breaks the promise in the comment at `src/Distribution.sol:146`. Three agents found it, and two reproduced it with scratch Foundry tests outside the repo. One test shows the clone needs about 4,170 gas even when the implementation is warm. It is listed twice, under `receive` and under `DistributionFactory.create`, because the skill does not merge findings across functions.
- **A token with two addresses (80, Medium).** On a chain like Celo, where the native coin also has an ERC-20 address, calling `distribute` with the ERC-20 address pays out shares already set aside for a beneficiary whose payment failed (`src/Distribution.sol:155`).
- **ERC-20 payments have no gas cap (75, Medium).** A beneficiary with an ERC-777-style receive hook can make `distribute` fail for every caller of that token (`src/Distribution.sol:417`). It is listed under both `distribute` and `_push`.
- **The clone address does not commit to its settings (75, Medium).** Whoever holds the salt key can deploy the clone on a new chain with their own owner and table, and take funds already sent to that address. The checks first marked this down because only the salt holder can do it; three agents agreeing promoted it back.

Two Low findings were also promoted because several agents raised them: a balance that drops below the held-back amount makes `distribute` revert, and anyone can run matured queued changes in any order.

App.sol and both deploy scripts produced no findings.

Three judgment calls the reconciler should know about:
- **Promotions to 75.** Three of the findings above reached 75 only through the skill's multi-agent promotion rule. I would defend two of them, the balance-below-reserve one and the `applyQueued` one, only as Low.
- **The `create` stipend fix is an outline.** Its diff describes the new clone code but does not write the bytecode.
- **One fix is partial.** The fix for the balance-below-reserve finding only swaps the crash for a clear revert. It does not share the loss fairly between beneficiaries.
